query: For high-entropy alloys intended for structural applications, what testable methodological hypothesis could enable improved combinations of strength, ductility, Young’s modulus, and fracture resistance? Explain why it should work, what measurable improvement is expected relative to the state of the art, the conditions under which it should or should not hold, the prior evidence supporting it, and an experimental result that would decisively falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: Controlled aging of equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi HEA at 650 °C for 10 h will produce ~3 vol% nanoscale coherent L12 γ′ precipitates that simultaneously increase yield strength and fracture toughness by >10% with minimal loss of ductility or modulus.
generation.material_initial_state: Solution‐treated equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi HEA, homogenized, grain size ~20 µm
generation.intervention: Isothermal aging at 650 °C (923 K) for 10 h in inert atmosphere
generation.conditions: Aging T = 600–700 °C; aging time ≤10 h; alloy composition within ±2 at.% of equiatomic; inert or vacuum environment
generation.structural_mediator: ~3 vol% coherent γ′ (L12) precipitates, size 20–50 nm
generation.mechanism: Precipitate strengthening via Orowan bowing impedes dislocation motion and blunts crack tips, raising strength and toughness
generation.predicted_outcome: Yield strength +20±5%, UTS +15±5%, fracture toughness +10±3%, ductility loss <5%, Young’s modulus change <2% relative to baseline
generation.baseline: Solution‐treated state: yield ~300 MPa, UTS ~550 MPa, KIC ~60 MPa√m, elongation ~50%, E ~200 GPa
generation.boundary: Holds for equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi aged 600–700 °C ≤10 h; fails if T>700 °C, time>20 h, or Cr>15 at.% causing secondary phase formation
generation.uncertainty: Moderate—extrapolated from Ni‐based superalloy data; limited direct HEA precipitation studies

falsification_experiment.design: Process two sets of CoCrFeMnNi HEA: (1) solution‐treated as baseline, (2) aged at 650 °C for 10 h. Characterize precipitate size/volume by TEM and perform tensile and fracture toughness tests under identical loading.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If aged specimens do not exhibit ≥10% increase in yield strength or ≥5% increase in KIC versus solution‐treated baseline, hypothesis is falsified.
